startup.name: Stormy
startup.one_liner: Runs the office so your crew can run the work
startup.description: AI back office for field and equipment service shops such as forklift and heavy equipment service, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, roofing and logistics yards. It answers calls day and night, follows up on quotes, books jobs, schedules crews, tracks parts, sends and collects invoices, runs marketing and gives each team member an AI agent, all from one job record. Five person team in San Francisco, Summer 2025.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent range). Up for a clear paying buyer in trades, AI timing and a product that already spans the job record. Down because the founders' domain background is not stated and the space has several funded trades AI companies. Net about 3 percent, conditional on the batch already given.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say that AI for trades is a crowded theme with many agents from the same batches, and that a bundle across call answering, scheduling and invoicing lacks a single sharp wedge. Partners may also doubt whether a five person team can integrate with the dominant field service software.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 16.3 months from 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17 and the number is for a round above about 1M from outside investors inside that window, not ever. Anchor 0.59 (B2B 2022 to 2025). About 85 percent of eventual seeds close within 16 months (p75 14.2), giving 0.50; 0.52 is 0.88x of the anchor. The hot AI agent theme and a five person team are not lifted above the anchor, per the winners test. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under 3M, the most common outcome for a small team that closes a first outside round quickly.
Institutional seed near the 2022 and later YC median of 4.1M, with market pre money near 18M.
Strong seed led by a known fund, matching the upper quartile of 6.5M and above in press covered rounds.
Large hot category round; rare for a team this early.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step fails if the broad bundle of call answering, quoting, scheduling, invoicing and marketing reads as a feature list with no deep win in any one job. Trades AI is crowded: Elyos, Sameday, Drillbit and Decisional all sell similar agents, and funded ServiceTitan, Jobber and Housecall Pro add their own AI. A five person team with a wide scope may show thin retention to investors.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C inside 16 months of YC is almost unseen even among the fastest AI voice companies, which needed rounds of tens of millions at Series B first. This team would need an unusual run of revenue growth across several trades, and no analog shows it.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely the company stays a small SaaS with churn in a seasonal customer base, or is absorbed by a field service platform that adds the same AI, the fate of several earlier trades startups. Breakout needs one trade where it becomes the system of record, where funded leaders already compete.

analogs.relevance: AI operating system for home services.
analogs.outcome_summary: Reached series B on voice AI.

killers.risk: Field service platforms add the same AI
killers.evidence: ServiceTitan, Jobber and Housecall Pro all ship or integrate AI receptionists, and guides say a native tool sees live technician availability.
killers.mitigation: Serve equipment service shops the platforms do not target.

killers.evidence: The pitch spans calls, quotes, scheduling, invoicing and marketing, and funded peers choose one job such as the voice agent.
killers.mitigation: Lead with one job that pays back in weeks.

killers.evidence: Trades shops are small, price sensitive and seasonal; Kanda and GoBuild failed in this buyer group.
killers.mitigation: Sell annual contracts to larger shops.

killers.evidence: Each product area needs integrations that larger rivals fund with many engineers.

competition_now.name: Trades native voice agents such as Avoca, Sameday and Rosie
competition_now.what: AI receptionists and booking agents for trades

competition_now.name: Answering services and an office manager
competition_now.what: Status quo of staff and call centers

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice agents and scheduling are buildable by a small team using current models. The hard part is integrations with field service and accounting software and reliable booking, which also forms the moat if solved. A bundle spanning marketing and invoicing raises the build load.

takeover_risk.rationale: Platforms already own the job record and distribution and can add agents quickly; funded voice startups are also expanding into the same functions.

evidence.claim: Vendor sources report 30 to 50 percent of inbound calls to trades shops go unanswered, a measurable loss.
Guides list a dozen paid AI receptionists for HVAC and plumbing, showing buyers pay.

actions: Measure calls answered and jobs booked
roadmap.proof: Ten paying shops with a booked job lift.

roadmap.goal: Prove retention and one clear wedge.
actions: Integrate with the main field service system
roadmap.proof: Monthly recurring revenue growing with under 3 percent monthly churn.

pros.point: Clear paying buyer and measurable loss
pros.evidence: Missed calls cost trades shops jobs, and buyers already pay for answering tools.

pros.point: Full job record gives a path to system of record
pros.evidence: The pitch runs every task off one job record, which can lock in customers.

brand.name: Stormy
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Stormy" --era 2022+: length bucket 5-6, 2 syllables, alive 93.7 percent in bucket, no signal.
brand.rationale: A short evocative name is easy to recall like Jobber, and a crew facing storms and emergencies may relate, but the word also hints at chaos. Name is secondary to execution in this crowded category.

narrative.headline: A broad AI back office for trades in the most crowded AI category: seed is about even over 16 months, later rounds are unlikely in the window.
narrative.general_summary: Stormy sells an AI back office to field and equipment service shops, from call answering and quoting through scheduling, parts and invoicing. The window is 16.3 months from 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17, long enough for most seeds, so seed sits at 0.52 against the B2B anchor of 0.59. Series A given seed is 0.07 in the window. Several funded trades AI companies and field service platforms compete directly. The odds do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2025-07-07 using only the input.
Seed means above about 1M from outside investors inside the 16.3 month window.
Founder backgrounds are not in the input and no domain advantage is assumed.
